{
  "findings": [
    {
      "title": "Primary endpoint hypothesis is two-sided but sample size justification implies one-sided",
      "quote": "H0: pCR rate = 25% Ha: pCR rate ≠ 25%",
      "page": 16,
      "section": "Statistical Plan",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "critical",
      "explanation": "The hypothesis is stated as two-sided (≠), but the sample size is calculated to reject the null if the true rate is 44%, which is a one-sided alternative. The protocol does not clarify whether a one-sided or two-sided test is used, which affects the alpha allocation and interpretation.",
      "fix": "Specify whether the primary analysis uses a one-sided or two-sided test and align the hypothesis and sample size calculation accordingly."
    },
    {
      "title": "Sample size calculation uses 72 patients but enrollment target is 76 with unclear accounting",
      "quote": "Seventy-two (72) patients will be required to provide 90% power... The sample size will be further increased by 5% to account for patients who prematurely withdraw (total sample size of approximately 76 patients).",
      "page": 16,
      "section": "Statistical Plan",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "72 increased by 5% is 75.6, which rounds to 76, but the protocol does not explain how the 5% inflation is applied or whether the 76 includes the 5% dropout. Also, the text says 'approximately 76' but the sample size section says 72 required, creating ambiguity about the final enrollment number.",
      "fix": "Clarify the exact sample size (e.g., 76) and how the 5% dropout is incorporated, and ensure consistency between the synopsis and body."
    },
    {
      "title": "Interim analysis section contradicts itself regarding no interim analysis",
      "quote": "No interim analysis is planned for the primary endpoint. After all patients have completed Part 1 of the study, an interim clinical study report (CSR) may be written to describe the analysis results for the primary endpoint.",
      "page": 16,
      "section": "Statistical Plan",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The text first states no interim analysis is planned, then describes an interim CSR that would analyze the primary endpoint. This is contradictory and could lead to misinterpretation about whether an interim analysis will be conducted.",
      "fix": "Clarify whether the interim CSR is a formal interim analysis or just a descriptive report, and specify any stopping or decision rules if it is an interim analysis."
    },
    {
      "title": "Primary endpoint definition lacks specification of pCR assessment timing and evaluable population",
      "quote": "The primary endpoint is pCR rate assessed by independent central pathology review.",
      "page": 15,
      "section": "Endpoint(s)",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The protocol does not define the exact timing of pCR assessment (e.g., after all neoadjuvant doses) or the population for the primary analysis (e.g., all enrolled vs. those who underwent surgery). This is critical for the estimand and analysis.",
      "fix": "Define the estimand for the primary endpoint, including the population, timing, and handling of patients who do not undergo surgery."
    },
    {
      "title": "Inconsistent statement about surgery timing for patients who discontinue early",
      "quote": "If a patient meets criteria to discontinue cemiplimab during the 12-week neoadjuvant period, the treating physician may divert the patient to surgery at an earlier time.",
      "page": 14,
      "section": "Study Part 1 (Neoadjuvant)",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The protocol does not specify the minimum or maximum time from last dose to surgery for early discontinuation, nor how this affects the primary endpoint assessment. This could introduce variability in pCR assessment.",
      "fix": "Specify the allowed window for early surgery and how it is handled in the analysis (e.g., as a sensitivity analysis)."
    },
    {
      "title": "Contraception requirements are missing entirely",
      "quote": "Women of childbearing potential will additionally undergo serum β-human chorionic gonadotropin (HCG) testing.",
      "page": 16,
      "section": "Procedures and Assessments",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "critical",
      "explanation": "The protocol mentions pregnancy testing but does not specify contraception requirements for men or women, which is essential for a drug like cemiplimab with potential teratogenicity. This is a regulatory and ethical gap.",
      "fix": "Add a detailed contraception section specifying requirements for both male and female participants, duration, and acceptable methods."
    },
    {
      "title": "No definition of 'aesthetically sensitive region' for stage II eligibility",
      "quote": "selected patients with stage II CSCC (≥3 cm longest diameter in an aesthetically sensitive region)",
      "page": 14,
      "section": "Study Design",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The term 'aesthetically sensitive region' is not defined, which could lead to inconsistent enrollment across sites and difficulty in determining eligibility.",
      "fix": "Define 'aesthetically sensitive region' with specific anatomical locations or provide examples."
    },
    {
      "title": "End of study definition is ambiguous regarding follow-up duration",
      "quote": "The end of study is defined as the last visit of the last patient.",
      "page": 15,
      "section": "End of Study Definition",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The definition is standard but does not specify whether the last visit includes the 3-year follow-up or if patients are followed until recurrence, which could make the end of study date unpredictable.",
      "fix": "Clarify that the end of study is the last visit of the last patient, including follow-up, and specify the maximum study duration."
    }
  ]
}
